mainEntity.name: How much does a Volvo S60 or V60 T5 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fully rebuilt B4204T11 engine for a Volvo S60 or V60 T5 typically costs £2,200-£3,500 supply-only or £3,000-£4,500 fitted. Used units start from £700, and reconditioned options sit between £1,400-£2,400. The five-cylinder B5254T12 is similar at £2,000-£3,200, while the T6 B4204T9 is higher at £2,800-£4,500. T4 (B4204T19) is the cheapest to replace - £1,800-£3,000. Polestar (B4204T43) is the most expensive - £3,500-£5,500. All EnginesMarket quotes include 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of PCV failure on an S60 or V60 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of PCV system failure include: oil leaks from camshaft seals or crankshaft seals, blue smoke from the exhaust on startup, a whistling noise from the engine, and increased oil consumption. The PCV system should be replaced every 60,000 miles as preventative maintenance. Ignoring PCV issues can starve the turbocharger of oil, causing catastrophic turbo failure. A simple "glove test" (placing a rubber glove over the oil filler cap opening) can indicate PCV blockage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Volvo S60 or V60 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2010-2015 S60 or V60 worth £3,000-£8,000, a £2,500-£4,500 engine replacement is borderline unless the vehicle is in exceptional condition with low mileage. For vehicles worth over £5,000, replacement is typically viable if the rest of the car is sound. Volvo petrol engines are known for longevity when properly maintained. Compare the cost of a rebuilt unit with warranty vs. buying another used car. We always recommend a specialist inspection before any decision.

mainEntity.name: How reliable is the Volvo S60 or V60 T5 petrol engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B4204T11 Drive-E T5 and the five-cylinder B5254T are generally considered reliable. With proper maintenance (PCV system every 60k miles, timing belt every 80k miles on five-cylinders, regular oil changes), many S60 and V60 petrols exceed 150,000 miles without major engine failure. Direct-injection engines require regular carbon cleaning (walnut blasting) every 60k-80k miles. PCV system neglect is the single biggest cause of premature failure. The five-cylinder B5254T is one of Volvo's most durable engines.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volvo S60 or V60 petrol engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full engine replacement on an S60 or V60 typically takes 3-5 working days for a specialist (5-7 days for a main dealer). PCV system replacement is typically a 1-day job. Timing belt replacement is 1-2 days. Carbon cleaning (walnut blasting) is 1-2 days. Supply & fit providers may offer courtesy vehicle options.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the T4, T5, and T6 petrol engines in the S60 and V60?

acceptedAnswer.text: The T4 is a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder producing 190hp. The T5 is a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder (Drive-E) producing 245hp, or a 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbo producing 254hp (older models). The T6 is a 2.0-litre twin-charged (supercharger + turbocharger) four-cylinder producing 306hp, or a 3.0-litre straight-six turbo producing 304hp (older models). The T6 is the most powerful and complex - higher running costs. The T4 is the most economical and cheapest to maintain. The T5 offers the best balance of performance and running costs.

historyTimeline.h2: Volvo S60 V60 T4 T5 T6 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volvo S60 and V60 have been offered with a range of petrol engines across two generations. The first generation (2000-2009 for S60, 2010-2018 for V60) featured Volvo's durable five-cylinder and six-cylinder turbocharged units - the B5254T family and the B6304T straight-six. The second generation (2019-present for S60, 2018-present for V60) introduced the Drive-E four-cylinder family (B4204Txx) with turbocharged and twin-charged configurations. This page covers all T4, T5 and T6 petrol variants across both body styles and generations.

commonProblems.h2: Volvo S60 V60 T4 T5 T6 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: Volvo's petrol engines - whether the five-cylinder B5254T, the straight-six B6304T, or the modern Drive-E B4204T family - are generally robust. However, age, mileage, and specific design characteristics bring predictable failure points. The most common issues across all variants are PCV system clogging, timing belt/chain wear, and carbon deposits on intake valves. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: PCV System Failure - Why Volvo S60 V60 Petrol Engines Develop Oil Leaks and Turbo Problems
problems.affectedModels: Volvo S60 V60 T4 T5 T6 petrol (all engine codes, particularly B5254T and B4204T families)
problems.rootCause: The PCV (Positive Crankcase Ventilation) system becomes blocked with sludge, increasing crankcase pressure. This forces oil past seals, leading to oil leaks from camshaft seals and crankshaft seals, and can starve the turbocharger of oil. Symptoms include oil leaks, blue smoke from the exhaust, and a whistling noise from the turbo. On the five-cylinder B5254T engines, PCV failure is the most common cause of turbocharger failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete PCV box, hoses and oil trap replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended every 60k miles; prevents turbo failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: PCV system plus turbocharger health check and oil feed cleaning

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt engine with new PCV, timing components, upgraded parts
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo has failed catastrophically or engine has been damaged

PCV system replacement (£350-£550) is well within value for any running example. A full engine replacement (£2,500-£4,500) makes sense for vehicles worth £5,000+ where the owner intends to keep the car for 2+ years. For sub-£3,000 examples with catastrophic engine failure, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: The PCV system is the single most important preventative maintenance item on all Volvo petrol engines covered here. If you own an S60 or V60 approaching 60,000 miles, budget for PCV replacement - it's far cheaper than a turbocharger or full engine replacement. The "glove test" (placing a rubber glove over the oil filler cap opening) can indicate PCV blockage.

problems.h4: Timing Belt / Chain Failure - Interference Engine Risk on S60 V60 Petrol Models
problems.affectedModels: Volvo S60 V60 petrol (all B5254T five-cylinder; B4204T Drive-E engines use timing chains)
problems.rootCause: The five-cylinder B5254T engines use a timing belt that must be replaced at 80,000 miles or 8 years - they are interference engines, meaning belt failure causes catastrophic valve damage. The Drive-E B4204T engines use a timing chain, which is generally more durable but can suffer tensioner wear on higher-mileage examples. Symptoms include rattling on startup (chain) or visible belt cracking.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Belt, tensioner, idler pulley, water pump replacement

repairOptions.longevity: If rattling on startup is detected

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Cylinder head rebuild with new valves, guides
repairOptions.longevity: If belt has snapped but bottom end is undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt engine with new timing components
repairOptions.longevity: If belt failure has caused bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Timing belt replacement (£400-£650) is a routine maintenance cost - it's well within value for any running S60 or V60. For vehicles with a snapped belt, the repair cost (£1,800-£3,200) may approach the value of sub-£3,000 examples.
problems.recommendation: Do not skip the timing belt service on five-cylinder models. The 80,000-mile or 8-year interval is non-negotiable. If you don't have documented belt history on a used car, budget for immediate replacement. For Drive-E chain engines, address any startup rattle promptly - tensioner failure is cheaper to fix than a full engine rebuild.

problems.h4: Carbon Deposits on Intake Valves - Direct-Injection Petrol Engine Issue
problems.affectedModels: Volvo S60 V60 T4 T5 T6 petrol (all B4204T Drive-E engines; some B5254T engines)
problems.rootCause: Direct injection petrol engines do not have fuel washing over the intake valves, leading to carbon buildup from crankcase ventilation gases. This can cause rough idle, reduced performance, and increased fuel consumption. This is a well-known issue across many direct-injection petrol engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Intake manifold removed, valves cleaned with walnut media

repairOptions.longevity: If carbon buildup has caused valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Carbon cleaning (£350-£600) is well within value for any S60 or V60 worth £3,000+.
problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is a maintenance item, not a catastrophic failure. Budget for walnut blasting every 60,000-80,000 miles on Drive-E engines. Using premium fuel and regular oil changes can help reduce the rate of buildup.
